text: Hello, everyone.Welcome to my class.Today, we are going to start a new journey as we approach the reading and interaction parts of United States of America.Today, we are going to start a new journey as we approach the reading and interaction parts of Unit 1, the media and the message.At the end of this period, you are expected toOne, understand the main idea and the structure of the text through skimming.Two, have a clear idea of the key points, including the definition of citizen journalism, its benefits, as well as potential dangers through scanning.Three, guess the meanings of the new words in the context.Now, please get your textbook and the worksheet ready.Okay, let's get started.Before we read the text, let me ask you a question.How do you hear about news story?In other words, what are your sources of news story?Obviously, nowadays, apart from the traditional means like newspaper, radio and TV, you can access news via blogs, news sites, news apps, not to mention other social media platforms.Is it a blessing or a curse?Are the news stories posted on social media sites reliable?That's what we are going to find out today in the text now in the news.Now, please skim the text and match each paragraph with the corresponding summary of its main idea.You will have one minute for it.Obviously, nowadays, apart from the traditional means like newspaper, radio and TV, you can access news sites, news apps, not to mention other social media platforms.Now, time is up.Let's check the answer.Paragraph 1 centers upon the reporting of the 2011 earthquake in Japan on social media.Paragraph 2 talks about the rise of citizen journalism on social media.Paragraph 3 talks about the change in the content of news produced by citizen journalists.Paragraph 4 talks about the unique value of citizen journalism.Paragraph 5 discusses the ethical problems of citizen journalism with two examples.In the last paragraph, as a conclusion, the writer touches upon the outlook for citizen journalism with a friendly reminder that we should reflect upon how to optimize the online environment we've got.Obviously, the topic for discussion here is citizen journalism.Let's dig deeper by going into the details of each paragraph.Now, please read the first paragraph and answer the following questions.You will have 30 seconds to find the answers.Shall we discuss the questions now?Question number one.What happened in Japan on the 11th of March 2011?On that fateful day, a massive earthquake hit Japan, followed by a huge tsunami.Then, what was the devastating scene like?The earthquake was a strong one, and the scene was terrible.The quake rocked the city, and the tsunami swept the coastline.You can see that in the picture.Can you guess the meaning of sweep here?Yes, it means to move suddenly and with force over an area.In Chinese, 席卷.What a vivid description here.Then, question number three.Who first reported the earthquake on social media sites?Actually, the people in the center of the disaster first reported it.To escape being swept away by tsunami, they climbed up bridges and buildings.At the same time, they continued to film with their smartphones and posted footage on their favorite social media sites.Footage means part of a film showing a particular event.In Chinese, 片段鏡頭.Actually, we call such people citizen journalists.They posted footage about the news of the quake first.Do you know when the footage appeared on social media?Yes, at 2.That's when media users heard about the news.It was shortly after the quake hit.Why are these citizen journalists able to post news stories more quickly than professional journalists?Now, please read paragraph two and try to find the answer.Have you got the answer?The speed is attributed to two reasons.One reason is that they are present at the scene of the particular event.And the other is that mobile technology enables them to film, post, and share the news quickly online.Now, I'm going to challenge you with a more demanding task.Based on the information from the first two paragraphs, please give a definition to citizen journalists.You will have 20 seconds for it.To define citizen journalists, we need to know who act as journalists and what they do.So, citizen journalists are ordinary individuals or non-professionals who collect, report, and analyze news and information, or post videos, photos, and commentaries on websites, blogs, or social media.When comparing citizen journalism and professional journalism, the difference is obvious in terms of the news writers, the devices used, and the speed of delivering the news story.Unlike professional journalists, citizen journalists are ordinary people who don't have training in the field of journalism.And they use smartphones to film the news, which are handy, but they are often able to deliver first-hand real-time stories really quickly.Apart from these aspects, what other differences lie between citizen journalism and professional journalism?Please read the third paragraph and find out.You will have one minute to fill in the form.Please fill in the form.Okay, time is up.At the beginning of the paragraph, the content by citizen journalists is described as being more personal and emotionally appealing.Though content by professional journalists may not be as appealing, it is often more objective, probably because background information as well as a broad overview are provided.That's what citizen journalism lacks.Actually, content differs greatly on a large part due to the procedure of how news is gathered and presented.Citizen journalists seldom cite reliable sources, and they have no time to collect and examine facts or explore the bigger picture.They just upload the content as they like.They don't bother to cite reliable sources.They seldom check whether the facts are true or not.No wonder their news story is less objective.By contrast, professional journalists not only need to cite sources, they have to make investigations to make sure the story is true.The table shows clearly the differences between citizen journalism and professional journalism, each type having some distinctive features.Despite the fact that news by citizen journalists is less objective, citizen journalism has great values, bringing great benefits.Now please read paragraph 4 and complete the chart.I will give you one minute for it.Please read paragraph 4 and complete the chart.Come it up.The chart here is for your reference.As you can see, citizen journalism supports and facilitates journalism, whose aim is to report news.At the individual level, ordinary people can benefit from it by telling their own stories, stories that matter to them, or stories that may lead to improved living standards.At the collective level, communities and groups can benefit from it.Stories about places previously unheard of can spread across the globe through the Internet.For example, some local communities are able to get the necessary help and assistance to develop local economy and be lifted out of poverty.Everything has two sides.It is the same with citizen journalism.What are the problems regarding citizen journalism?Please read from line 69 to line 76 in the fifth paragraph and locate some keywords.You may find two words which are strong accusations here, unregulated and no accountability.Unregulated means not controlled or supervised by rules or principles.The adjective form of accountability is accountable.It means responsible for your decisions or actions and expected to explain them when you are asked.When there is no rule to govern how citizen journalists should go about doing their reporting, no system in place to make sure they are held accountable for his or her reporting, the consequences are bound to cause tremendous harm and affect people's lives.How are people's lives affected by unconfirmed stories posted by citizen journalists?Please read the two case stories in paragraph five and filling the table as required.You will have two minutes for it.Please read the two cases stories in paragraph five and filling the table as required.OK, time is up.Please check the information you've got against the mind here on the screen.The first news story posted is about an extremely dangerous online game which was popular among teenagers around the world.Then the hoax went viral and made headlines in big newspapers in several countries.It is a hoax because the truth is that the game didn't even exist.So hoax means a false report, but still it spread very quickly and became a central focus.So go viral means spread quickly and make headlines means to be the most important items of news.As for the hoax, the fake news caused unnecessary fear and panic among parents worldwide, and the police department used limited resources to investigate the false claim.It is a huge waste of public resources and the taxpayers' money, which could otherwise have been used to make headlines.As for the second case, the online news story goes like this.A 16-year-old girl mysteriously disappeared and was very likely kidnapped.Kidnapping is a crime.Can you guess the meaning here?It means taking someone away illegally and with force in Chinese police force.After the story spread across the Internet, social media users started the online campaign Help Find Kara, and 34,000 people shared the message.But unfortunately, the truth is that it is a scam.A scam is a clever and dishonest plan to treat others, For we know, Kara was eventually located by the police and brought back home.She faked her own kidnapping.The harm done is far and wide.It's wasted a lot of people's time and energy.And also, it hurts innocent people's feelings.After all, it's a scam.After all, to use the words in the text, everyone believed Kara's story and fell for the scam.The scam cast a shadow on people's minds.Do you think in the future, these kind-hearted people will easily trust others and readily help as they did this time?So, some harm is visible.Some is invisible.But very often, the psychological and emotional wounds are harder to heal.Do you agree?So far, you have gained a lot of information about citizen journalism, its good side as well as its downside.What does the future hold for citizen journalists?Please read the last paragraph and find out the answers to the questions you have.You will have 20 seconds.What's the outlook for citizen journalism?Citizen journalism is an unstoppable trend.It will continue to develop as a relatively new phenomenon.Citizen journalists will continue to film and post stories online.What should we do faced with the changing media environment?Make the best use of the media, which is what we should do.After skimming and scanning the text, you are supposed to have a clear picture of citizen journalism.Now please think about this question.Is citizen journalism a good or a bad thing from the long-term perspective?You will have two minutes to think about it.What's the future for citizen journalism?Too many cooks spoil the soup.Maybe it is the same with journalism.According to Edison, citizen journalism is not well regulated, so if it is taken advantage of by bad people, the consequence will be very serious.All your ideas are very impressive.I hope the discussion will remind you to always view things in an objective way, which means being open-minded and looking at things from multiple sides.Now comes the interactive task.Please discuss with your group members and find more differences between citizen journalism and professional journalism.Now we've come to the end of today's lesson.Here are your assignments.Listen to the audio recording of the text and read the text at least twice.Finish comprehension work 1 and 2 on page 8 in the textbook.Thank you for attending my class.See you next time.
